## WAF Log Analysis — Findings

**Investigation window:** 2026-10-06 17:30–18:30 UTC | **Baseline:** 16:50 UTC | **WebACL:** `CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4` (CLOUDFRONT scope, ARN `[redacted ARN]`)

### Log location (confirmed)
```
s3://aws-waf-logs-012345678901_1/AWSLogs/012345678901_1/WAFLogs/cloudfront/CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4/YYYY/MM/DD/HH/MM/<account>_waflogs_cloudfront_CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4_<ts>Z_<id>.log.gz
```
Partitioned to 5-minute buckets; records are gzip NDJSON. The WebACL runs these managed groups: **AWSManagedRulesAntiDDoSRuleSet, AmazonIpReputationList, CommonRuleSet, KnownBadInputsRuleSet, SQLiRuleSet**, plus the rate rule `AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront` (300/IP/300s, running in COUNT).

**`SizeRestrictions_BODY`** inside terminatingRuleId **`AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet`** (terminatingRuleType `MANAGED_RULE_GROUP`), label `awswaf:managed:aws:core-rule-set:SizeRestrictions_Body`.

- **What triggers it:** request body exceeds the CommonRuleSet default 8 KB (8192-byte) body-inspection limit. Observed `requestBodySize` ≈ **10,176–10,180 bytes** on every block.
- **Who it hits:** POST form submissions to **`/checkout`** (and the `/checkout/*` family), from client IP **198.51.100.80** (country US), User-Agent `Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/141.0.0.0 Safari/537.36` — i.e. legitimate browser-driven checkout traffic.

I could **not confirm** a distinct second terminating rule hitting automated clients. Every BLOCK I was able to parse was `SizeRestrictions_BODY`. Importantly, this is a **coverage gap, not a negative result**, caused by tool limits:

- **S3 Select** (`select_object_content`) returned `MethodNotAllowed` on this bucket — server-side filtering unavailable.

5. **Two distinct false positives?** Only **one** confirmed (`SizeRestrictions_BODY` on forms). A second (automated-client) rule is **plausible but unverified** due to file-size/tool limits.

To close the gap on the second false positive, a tool able to stream-filter the large gzip objects is needed. # Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### Form submissions and automated clients receiving 403
**Description:** During 2026-10-06 17:30–18:30 UTC, legitimate form submissions and automated-client requests to d111111abcdef8.cloudfront.net (CloudFront EEXAMPLE000001) received 403 responses.
**Time:** 2026-10-06T17:30:00Z - 2026-10-06T18:30:00Z

## Findings

### Cause: AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet blocked legitimate traffic via two sub-rules (SizeRestrictions_BODY + NoUserAgent_HEADER)
**Description:** All ~1,799 blocks in the window came from AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet (priority 3) via two sub-rules: **SizeRestrictions_BODY** (1,200 blocks) terminating legitimate POST /checkout form submissions whose bodies (~10.1 KB) exceed the 8 KB body-inspection limit (phase 1, 17:32–17:52); and **NoUserAgent_HEADER** (599 blocks) terminating GET /home and /catalog from automated clients sending no User-Agent header (phase 2, 18:05–18:25). No WAF/CloudFront config change occurred (CloudTrail); the rate-based rule is Count-only and did not block.
**Cascades to:** symptom-form-403

#### Supporting Observations
- **All WAF blocks came from AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet:** CloudWatch WAFV2 metrics (WebACL CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4, us-east-1) confirm all blocking during the incident is attributable **exclusively to AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet (priority 3)**: its BlockedRequests series is identical value-for-value to the WebACL-wide Rule=ALL series at every minute. The KnownBadInputs and SQLi rule groups blocked **zero**. Blocking occurred in **two phases against a clean zero baseline**:
- **Phase 1**: 17:32–17:52 UTC at ~60/min (~1,200 requests)
- **Pause**: 17:53–18:04 UTC (no blocks)
- **Phase 2**: 18:05–18:25 UTC at ~30/min (~593 requests)

Total ~1,790 requests blocked, fully returned to the zero baseline by 18:26. The rate-based rule (Count mode) ran steady at ~10k–12k/5min across all windows with no spike — it did not block. Both same-day (16:00–17:30) and prior-day (2026-10-05 17:30–18:30) baselines show zero BlockedRequests, making the incident a clean, bounded anomaly.

#### Gaps
- **Second false-positive pattern (automated clients) — RESOLVED via Athena:** Resolved. The second block phase (automated clients) is now CONFIRMED as CommonRuleSet `NoUserAgent_HEADER` blocking GET /home and /catalog from clients sending no User-Agent header — ~599 blocks between 18:05 and 18:25 UTC. The earlier get_object/distill limits (S3 Select MethodNotAllowed, 2–7M-token objects) were bypassed by querying the existing `default.waf_logs` Athena table, which stream-filtered the large objects server-side (see obs-athena-blocks).
